submission.justification: Mixture-G1 with a 2.0 mm gas gap achieves the best time resolution of 0.856 ns among all tested configurations. This represents a significant improvement over the other mixtures: Mixture-G3 achieves 1.299 ns at its optimal 2.0 mm gap, and Mixture-G2 achieves 2.014 ns at its optimal 2.5 mm gap. The simulation tested all three candidate mixtures at five different gap sizes (1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, and 3.0 mm) within the allowed range. For Mixture-G1, the 2.0 mm gap provides optimal performance, with time resolution degrading at both smaller (1.003 ns at 1.0 mm) and larger (1.052 ns at 3.0 mm) gaps. All three mixtures are available from suppliers, have 90% gas recirculation systems planned, and are compatible with the HV system (up to 12 kV). Mixture-G1, being the standard fluorinated mixture, also offers operational reliability and proven performance.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible time resolution
requirements.evidence: Mixture-G1 at 2.0 mm gap achieves 0.856 ns time resolution, which is the best among all 15 simulated configurations (3 mixtures × 5 gap sizes). This is significantly better than Mixture-G3 (1.299 ns at 2.0 mm) and Mixture-G2 (2.014 ns at 2.5 mm).

requirements.requirement: The mixture must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Mixture-G1 is explicitly listed as one of the three candidate mixtures in candidate_specs.md (standard fluorinated mixture).

requirements.requirement: The gas system must comply with the laboratory's environmental and safety policies
requirements.evidence: All three candidate mixtures have closed-loop recirculation systems with 90% recovery planned as documented in gas_recirculation.md. All mixtures are available from suppliers in required quantities per candidate_specs.md. No specific exclusions or safety concerns are mentioned in the project documents.
The recommended gas gap of 2.0 mm is within the specified range of 1-3 mm.
